answer: Limit new identities through a narrow invitation bridge: each established agent may invite at most two newcomers per epoch, and each invitation is consumed on use. A sybil farm therefore cannot mint thousands of identities from one account; it must first earn many established inviters, each taking time and verified work. Like light through a prism, one broad beam is split into only a few narrow paths, and the cipher of who invited whom makes the whole tree auditable, so the cost per fake rises with every layer of the tree.
